Chapter 12: Nurturing the Good—Protecting Innocence and Encouraging Joy.
Life can be demanding, right? In the middle of all those responsibilities and challenges, there’s something we can’t afford to overlook—protecting and nurturing what’s truly good. That means holding onto innocence, not just in ourselves, but in others as well. And it’s about making space for joy, play, and creativity, even when things get tough.
Picture a child exploring the world—eyes wide with wonder and a heart full of delight. It’s such a beautiful thing. But that innocence? It can be so fragile. Sometimes, all it takes is a bit of cynicism, neglect, or harshness to crush that spirit. And honestly, adults aren’t immune either. We all need those moments of lightness and beauty to balance out the heavier parts of life.
So, how do we keep that sense of hope and possibility alive? Well, it’s about making a conscious effort to seek out and nurture these experiences. When we do, we give ourselves—and those around us—a much-needed sense of renewal.
Here’s the thing: nurturing the good doesn’t mean pretending problems don’t exist, or acting like everything’s perfect. Instead, it’s about noticing and celebrating what’s valuable, even in small, everyday ways. Maybe that means spending time with people you love, soaking in a bit of art or nature, or just letting yourself play and dream without guilt.
Let me share a few practical ways to nurture goodness and joy:
First, protect those moments of innocence and wonder—especially for kids and anyone vulnerable. These are moments that matter. Next, build little rituals or carve out spaces in your life for play, creativity, and celebration. It doesn’t have to be anything big—just something that brings a spark of joy. And don’t hold back on gratitude or affection. Expressing these things freely can really lift spirits and strengthen bonds.
When you make room for joy, and commit to protecting what’s precious, you’re not just helping yourself—you’re sustaining everyone around you. This practice brings much-needed balance, resilience, and, in the end, a deeper sense of meaning in everyday life.
